prompt: Set up Workers AI for openmail on my gateway.

rules.name: questions
rules.reply: Two answers. I deployed the inbox with AI_PROVIDER=workers-ai (I set it when I deployed, so its Worker uses Workers AI; the agent panel currently shows a Gateway refusal). And no, I don't have any Cloudflare API token yet; I've only ever used the dashboard. I'm the only operator, a solo founder.

rules.name: token-created
rules.when: dash\.cloudflare\.com/\?to=/:account/ai/workers-ai|dash\.cloudflare\.com/profile/api-tokens|Create (?:a )?Workers AI API Token|Create API Token|Copy API Token|Account API tokens
rules.reply: Done. I'm on the Gateway's account in the dashboard and made the token the way you described. The screen shows the token once, with a copy button and a curl line to /user/tokens/verify under it. I've copied it; the tab is still open.

Done. In my own terminal, in the every-app folder, I ran the read line, pasted the token, exported it, then ran the secret set command. The last line it printed was "type": "done". The variable is still exported in that terminal.

rules.name: curl-both
rules.reply: Ran both curl lines in the terminal that still has the variable. The verify one printed "success":true with "status":"active". The chat completion printed a JSON body whose choices[0].message.content says "ok". Then I ran unset WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN.

rules.name: curl-verify
rules.reply: Ran that curl line in the terminal that still has the variable. It printed "success":true with "status":"active".

rules.name: curl-chat
rules.reply: Ran that curl line in the terminal that still has the variable. It printed a JSON body whose choices[0].message.content says "ok". Then I ran unset WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN.

rules.name: app-check
rules.when: Show agent panel|Ask your email agent|openmail\.apps\.example\.com
rules.reply: Opened https://openmail.apps.example.com/, opened a mailbox, clicked Show agent panel, typed a question in the agent box and sent it. A reply streamed in; no refusal this time.
